clue.text: Charity appeal that follows increase in seasonal fare

definitions.text: Charity appeal that follows increase in seasonal fare

parts.words: Charity appeal that follows increase in seasonal fare
parts.note: the seasonal fare is the Christmas goose, and the rhyme says that once the goose is getting fat, a begging line for the poor comes next

annotation.spelling: PLEASE PUT A PENNY IN THE OLD MAN'S HAT

explanation.surface: A fundraising request that comes after festive food prices go up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'increase in seasonal fare' sounds like a price rise but is the goose growing plump in the nursery rhyme 'Christmas is coming, the goose is getting fat', whose next line is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's second line is a plea for alms, literally a charity appeal following the fattening goose.

clue.text: Herb Simpson tumbled in grass

indicators.note: in places the turned initials inside the coastal grass word

parts.note: marram is a coarse grass that binds sand dunes

indicators.note: tumbled means the initials fall over and are read backwards

parts.note: O.J. Simpson, the American footballer and actor, known by his initials

explanation.surface: Someone called Simpson fell over in the grass while picking herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumbled' looks like an anagram signal, but it only turns the initials round; the grass is marram, a dune grass less familiar than the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Marjoram is an aromatic culinary plant of the mint family, a common kitchen herb.

clue.text: What my dog may do when I go out

indicators.note: go out suggests the letters stepping out of line and coming back in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: My dog makes a fuss every time I leave the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when I go out' reads as the time of the dog's complaint, but 'go out' is the anagram signal on WHEN I.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog left alone often makes a high plaintive cry, the thing a pining pet does.

clue.text: Local legwear that is scrubbed for Terry

indicators.note: is scrubbed for means one piece is wiped out and another put in its place

parts.note: hosiery is stockings and tights, legwear collectively
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is' (id est)
Tel is a British nickname for someone called Terry

explanation.surface: Stockings are being washed for a man named Terry down the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for one's nearby pub. Remove IE ('that is') from HOSIERY and put TEL in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage your local is the nearby pub, and a hostelry is an inn or pub.

clue.text: Top-level luminary keeps hide for writing

indicators.note: keeps means the phrase holds the answer within its letters, running across the words

explanation.surface: A great celebrity holds on to an animal skin on which to write.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through leVEL LUMinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Vellum is fine calfskin parchment, an animal hide prepared as a writing surface.

clue.text: It may be put in restaurant's pot pourri mixed with rose tip to mask pong

definitions.text: It may be put in restaurant's pot

indicators.note: to mask means the smell is covered up by being placed within the other letters
mixed tells us to jumble the letters of the fodder together
tip here is the end letter of the word rose

parts.note: pong is British slang for a bad smell, and BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A dish of scented petals is blended with a rose to cover a nasty smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' belongs to the definition, not to 'pourri'. 'mixed' rearranges POURRI with E (the tip of 'rose') into POURIRE, and 'to mask' puts BO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pourboire is French for a tip, the money left in a waiter's tips jar or pot.

clue.text: Glass-maker with degree builds Roman church

indicators.note: builds says the answer combined with the degree makes up the church, so take the degree away from it

parts.note: a basilica is a type of Roman church, such as St Peter's
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A glassmaker holding a university degree constructs a church in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the answer 'with' BA builds BASILICA, so the answer is BASILICA minus BA.
explanation.definitionFit: Silica, silicon dioxide as found in sand, is the main raw material from which glass is made.

clue.text: See 1
Beastly schoolmate misbehaved, caught out

indicators.note: misbehaved suggests letters acting up and running out of order
out means the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A nasty pupil behaved badly and was dismissed in a cricket game.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C ('caught', 'out') from SCHOOLMATE to leave SHOOLMATE, and rearrange those letters ('misbehaved').
explanation.definitionFit: Beastly and loathsome are synonyms, both describing something horrid or detestable.

clue.text: View missing page one: it'll make you weep

indicators.note: missing means these letters are absent from the longer word

parts.note: a view is an opinion
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An opinion piece without its first page is so sad it brings tears.
explanation.walkthrough: Take P and I out of OPINION.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping this vegetable releases a gas that irritates the eyes and makes people cry.

clue.text: Extra spinner with bounce essentially in turn

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the word for a performance

parts.note: a turn is a stage act
a DJ, disc jockey, spins records

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the central letters of the word bounce

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler adds extra bounce when it is his turn to bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' and 'bounce' suggest cricket, but the spinner is a DJ; UN is the middle of BOUNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjunct is an addition or supplementary thing, so it means an extra.

clue.text: A girl's ugly husband's rather big

indicators.note: ugly suggests the letters are made unsightly by being twisted out of shape

parts.note: girl's is taken with its S as part of the fodder
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: An unattractive girl's husband is fairly large.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange A GIRLS ('ugly') to get LARGIS and add H for husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Largish means fairly large, the same as rather big.

clue.text: Pound's variable during long period

indicators.note: during means the letter falls within the span of the time word

parts.note: an era is a long period of time
Z is a typical algebraic variable

explanation.surface: The value of the pound has fluctuated over a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like the currency but is the American poet Ezra Pound; 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The modernist poet Pound's first name is the definition's target, a name-for-surname clue.

clue.text: Dog collars cat in interminable mad hothouse production

indicators.note: collars means the dog goes around the other letters like a collar round a neck

parts.note: Pluto is Mickey Mouse's dog in the Disney cartoons

indicators.note: in places the tom inside the shortened word
interminable means without its end, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A dog grabs a cat inside a crazy endless greenhouse scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' and 'cat' read as a squabble in the surface; Pluto is Mickey Mouse's dog, and 'interminable' cuts the D from MAD to leave MA.
explanation.definitionFit: This large tomato variety is often grown under glass, so it is a greenhouse crop.

clue.text: Is he in the middle of nowhere at odds with creation?

definitions.text: Is he in the middle of nowhere at odds with creation?

indicators.note: at odds with suggests things in disagreement, out of order, so the letters are rearranged
the middle of picks out the central letter of the word nowhere

explanation.surface: Someone living in a remote spot asks whether he is out of step with the world.
explanation.walkthrough: H, the centre of 'nowhere', joins CREATION and the nine letters are rearranged. The whole clue also describes a hermit.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorite is a religious recluse who withdraws from the world to live remotely.

clue.text: Peacekeepers for the most part ceding current base

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are the United Nations forces

indicators.note: ceding means giving up, so this letter is surrendered from the word

parts.note: for the most part means mainly
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Peacekeeping forces mostly giving ground at their military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a military camp but is an adjective meaning dishonourable. MAINLY gives up I to leave MANLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmanly in its old sense means cowardly or ignoble, and base means mean-spirited or ignoble.

clue.text: Irish poet Russell considered effervescent

parts.note: George William Russell, the Irish poet, wrote under the pen name AE
considered, in the sense judged, means rated

explanation.surface: An Irish poet named Russell was thought lively and bubbly.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerated drinks have gas forced into them, making them fizzy or effervescent.

clue.text: Water-carrier died in a never-ending line at court

indicators.note: in means the letter for died goes inside the shortened line
never-ending means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a line of people waiting is a queue

explanation.surface: Someone carrying water died while standing in an endless queue at a court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never-ending' cuts the last E from QUEUE to leave QUEU; 'at' is a link word between the line and the court.
explanation.definitionFit: An aqueduct is a bridge or channel built to carry water across country.

clue.text: Seafood dishes or rump steak cooked with no rump

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters being prepared and mixed into a new dish
with no rump means the word loses its tail, its last letter

explanation.surface: Seafood or a rump steak prepared without the rump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rump' is used twice: once as fodder and once as 'tail'. STEAK loses its last letter K, and RUMPSTEA is rearranged ('cooked').
explanation.definitionFit: Tempura is Japanese battered and deep-fried food, very often prawns or other seafood.

clue.text: Rings about going to meet the King's No. 1

indicators.note: going means the letter departs from the word

parts.note: rings, as on the phone, means calls
C is short for circa, Latin for about
to hook up is to meet

explanation.surface: Someone phones about going to see Elvis's chart-topping hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The King is Elvis Presley. CALLS without C ('about going') gives ALLS, then HOOK UP.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1957 single was one of Elvis Presley's number-one hits, and he is known as the King.

clue.text: Irish novelist's devotee in Romanian capital

indicators.note: in means the fan goes inside the currency word

parts.note: capital here is money: the leu is the Romanian currency
a devotee is a fan

explanation.surface: An admirer of an Irish writer visits Bucharest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romanian capital' suggests Bucharest but means its money, the leu. 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan Le Fanu was a Victorian Irish author of gothic and ghost stories.

clue.text: When man quits monastery abroad he's tight-lipped

indicators.note: quits means these letters leave the longer word's pool of letters
abroad here means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: When a monk leaves an overseas monastery he says nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters M, A, N out of MONASTERY ('quits') to leave OSTERY, which is rearranged ('abroad').
explanation.definitionFit: A shellfish that keeps its shell clamped shut stands for a person who will not talk.

clue.text: She ends programme with a somersault

indicators.note: a somersault turns things head over heels, so the letters are read backwards
ends here picks out the closing letters of the word programme

explanation.surface: A woman finishes a show by doing a somersault.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of 'programme', AMME, is turned round; 'with a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a woman's name, so it can stand for 'she'.

clue.text: Old blend in Italy 2009

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy
2009 in Roman numerals is MMIX

explanation.surface: An old blend from Italy dating from 2009.
explanation.definitionFit: Immix is an archaic verb meaning to mix in or mingle, so it is an old word for blend.

clue.text: Struggles to make Betsy beefy, for instance

parts.note: the name Betsy becomes the word beefy when its T and S give way to E and F, and that swap written as an instruction is the answer

explanation.surface: Attempts to fatten up a girl named Betsy.
explanation.walkthrough: A letter-swap instruction: 'to make Betsy beefy' you put EF in place of TS, and 'EF for TS' run together is the answer; 'for instance' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Efforts are attempts or exertions, the same as struggles.

clue.text: I'm with my Roman counterpart, tucking into extremely dubious appetisers

indicators.note: tucking into means these letters go inside the outer letters
extremely picks the extreme letters, first and last, of the word dubious

parts.note: I'm without its apostrophe gives IM
the Latin, Roman, equivalent of 'I am' is sum

explanation.surface: Two people tuck into some questionable starters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my Roman counterpart' means the Latin for 'I am', the counterpart of 'I'm'; 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'dubious'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim sum are small Chinese dumplings and snacks served as light starters.

clue.text: Bad news for Wimbledon players?

parts.note: tennis players would be stuck without the mesh across the court; read differently, the players are nine musicians

explanation.surface: Tennis players getting bad news at Wimbledon.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO NET it is bad news for tennis players; as one word it is a group of nine musical players.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine musicians, the 'players' read in the musical sense.

clue.text: Point to kid eating one in each dish

indicators.note: in means the pieces go inside the abbreviation for each

parts.note: N, north, is a compass point

indicators.note: eating means the child swallows the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a kid is a child
A is one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone points a child towards a dish while they eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts A (one) inside CHILD to make CHILAD; 'to' is a link, and 'each' is abbreviated as it is in prices.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican dish, a tortilla rolled round a filling.
